data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A large centralized service is more resilient because it can implement 'synthetic diversity' and global orchestration that exceeds the capabilities of uncoordinated small services.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The orchestration layer itself becomes the single point of failure (the 'Resilience Paradox' in SCR_004).","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The cost of maintaining synthetic diversity outweighs the marginal gain in resilience.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"A centralized operator can intentionally deploy N different versions of its software, use different OS kernels across clusters, and implement global circuit breakers that detect the onset of a correlated failure in real-time.
